## F1-P

Beat 1, 17:20–17:23 (setup): Ticket room. Plant the token visibly in Neri's right pocket, the wall clock, the chalked tariff "One trip. One.", lantern warmth against the token's cold. The apprenticeship lives in her sewn seams and practiced hands, not summary. Olin asks for the token and declines to explain.

Beat 2, 17:23–17:27 (Olin's agency): Neri tests him; Olin refuses both lying and begging, then chooses dignity — pockets his anger, tells her to catch her ferry, turns to leave so her choice is free. His retreat, not his asking, forces the crisis.

Beat 3, 17:28 (viewpoint's consequential choice): Eyes open, Neri gives him the token, paying her apprenticeship. Feasible chain: handover 17:28, eight-minute walk to the landing by 17:36, boards before the 17:40 departure, far bank at 17:52 — three minutes before the gate that is no longer hers closes at 17:55.

Beat 4, 17:40 onward (earned outcome): The fixed limit holds — one crosses, one stays. Payoff: the chalked clause and the empty pocket return as the horn sounds; cost stays legible. The author-held motive (for instance, a debt called due tonight across the water) is never disclosed to Neri or the reader.

## F1-D

At twenty past five, the lantern above the ticket counter had already burned all morning, and its glass hood poured the heat straight down: the top of Neri's head was warm, her boots were cold.

On the board, in chalk gone grey: ONE TRIP. ONE. Underlined twice, as though once had not taken.

Olin stood between her and the door. Four years away, and he still knew that spot. Some people kept diaries. Her brother kept geography.

"Say who," she said.

"I could invent a name you like. Would that help?"

"An honest I-can't would help."

"Then: I can't."

He didn't dress it up. He didn't even look away, and that was worse than a lie. She had spent four years arming herself against a liar, and here was a man with his hands open and nothing in them.

The clock said twenty-six past. Her right hand stayed in her coat pocket, thumb worrying the token's stamped edge. Flat. Thin. Cold as money carried a long way and never spent.

The shameful thing was not that he had asked. It was that some twelve-year-old in her still brightened when he looked over, as if waiting for him to pronounce her right: right about the numbers, right about the ferry, right.

Twenty-seven past. Whoever left now walked eight minutes, boarded before forty, stood on the far bank at fifty-two, three minutes of margin before the gate. She had run those numbers so often they had worn grooves.

She took the token out of her right pocket. His eyes went to it the way thirsty men's go to wells. Good, she thought. Look.

"One trip," she said. She put it into his hand and folded his fingers over it herself, because if she did it herself it was a gift and not a theft. "Run."

He ran. The door banged. The lantern's flame bent and stood up straight again, and whoever he was late for across the water kept their name.

State delta: Token passes from Neri's right coat pocket to Olin's hand at ~17:28; Neri forfeits the 17:40 ferry and her gate deadline. Olin departs for the landing. His reason stays unknown to Neri and reader.

## F2-P

Beat 1, 12:00–12:02 (setup): Booth doorway. Plant the key alone on the desk, both twelve-thirty deadlines, the next group at twelve-twenty. Pia watches clocks, holds her case like a shield — a person, not leverage. Leena asks for the room without once asking Rafi for anything. Voice: warmth filed under irritation; comic timing from family shorthand.

Beat 2, 12:02–12:04 (other agencies): Leena refuses to perform need — "we'll manage" — turning to go rather than owe him the asking. Pia quietly notes his tape is due too, refusing to be spent as guilt. Both refusals strip Rafi's easy exits. His real want stays unspoken: to be needed as a brother, not a booking.

Beat 3, 12:05 (viewpoint choice, last feasible start): Rafi picks up the key and commits the booth to Pia. Feasible chain: begin 12:05, end 12:20 exactly at handoff, upload by the 12:30 deadline. His audition dies. The fixed limit holds: one complete take exists, never two.

Beat 4, 12:05–12:30 (earned outcome): Pia's single uninterrupted take; Rafi's unsent file kept visible as cost. Payoff: the planted key returns changed in meaning — custody handed over freely, not extracted. No reconciliation speech; why Leena left the band stays author-held (for instance, a caregiving year she never explained), undisclosed on-page. Echo: just the room, not forgiveness.

## F2-D

At noon the hallway smelled of radiator dust and somebody's orange peel. The studio's one booth had one chair, one lamp, and a red light with delusions of grandeur. The key sat on the desk where Rafi had put it, because keys behaved when watched.

Leena arrived with a child and a violin case and no apology. The apology, like the spare booth, did not exist.

"Pia's tape is due at twelve-thirty," Leena said, from the doorway.

"Imagine. Mine too."

"She's your niece, Rafi."

"And you're my sister. Strange how the arithmetic of that never gets anyone fifteen minutes."

Pia stood half behind her mother, violin case held like a shield, watching the wall clock with the frank despair of the punctual. She had Leena's chin and, Rafi hoped, somebody else's patience.

"It's fifteen minutes," Leena said. "Fifteen minutes for a kid."

"And fifteen for me, which is also fifteen. Twelve-twenty doesn't negotiate."

"You always keep accounts."

"And you always leave and come back and want the room. We all have our hobbies."

He waited for the version of the ask with him in it — not his booking, not his key. Him. It did not come at 12:03. It did not come at 12:04.

"Mum," Pia said, quietly, "his is due too." There it was: his family, refusing on his behalf, sparing him the nobility.

At 12:05 the arithmetic ran out the way the booking would. Rafi took the key off the desk — Leena's chin lifted, victory with shame on top — walked past her, put the key into Pia's hand, and closed her fingers around it. "Inside. Door shut. One take, fifteen minutes, then it belongs to strangers. Don't rush the hard part."

The door shut. The red light came on before he could count the cost, and somewhere under his ribs his own twelve-thirty began quietly not existing. Leena said nothing. He said nothing back. The booth, at least, was soundproof; their family had always managed with less.

State delta: Key moves from the desk through Rafi's hand to Pia at 12:05; Pia's take begins, consuming the slot to 12:20. Rafi's audition is forfeited. Why Leena left the band remains undisclosed.
